newsitem.title: CONGO: Airport battle sinks Congo truce, French assaulted.
newsitem.headline: Airport battle sinks Congo truce, French assaulted.

text.p: A ferocious battle for Brazzaville airport on Wednesday shredded Congo's week-old truce, sending hundreds of civilians fleeing.

Panicky troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba assaulted France's ambassador, beat up his bodyguard and shot at his escort as he tried to leave Lissouba's palace after a meeting, members of his entourage said.
Diplomats said Lissouba's foe, former president Denis Sassou Nguesso, appeared to have launched an assault on the city's strategically vital airport.
"It seems Sassou has taken at least part of the airport and created a new military situation which is making the government troops nervous," one said by telephone.

Shells slammed into the landmark high-rise Sofitel hotel beside the Congo river and landed around the nearby French embassy, just 200 metres (yards) on Lissouba's side of the frontline that divides the city.
Some 30 French nationals, mostly diplomats and gendarmes, took refuge in the embassy compound. The shelling boomed on into the early evening.

"Hundreds, maybe thousands of people are fleeing north and south to the edges of the city," international Red Cross (ICRC) spokesman Paolo Dell'Oca said in the twin capital of Kinshasa, just over the river in the former Zaire.

A pilot who was to have flown into Brazzaville said he was warned away by the control tower which said Sassou's "Cobra" militias had taken the Aeroclub, less than a kilometre (mile) from the main airport building.
The Aeroclub was base for 1,250 French troops who pulled out last week after evacuating thousands of foreign nationals.
A shaky week-old ceasefire had dampened but failed to stop clashes between Lissouba and Sassou, whose 12 days of battles erupted on June 5 and have left 1,000 to 3,000 people dead.
Wednesday's airport clash frayed nerves among Lissouba's regular army and his private "Zulu" militia fighting alongside.
Discipline evaporated at their roadblocks and even at the presidency itself, where diplomats heard officials screaming at each other.
French ambassador Raymond Cesaire, visiting Lissouba, was forced to retreat to the presidency when soldiers started assaulting him as he left, members of his entourage said.
His bodyguard was knockedt unconscious with a rifle and beaten. Soldiers fired three shots into an armoured saloon car carrying Cesaire's gendarme escorts, but no one was injured.
The United Nations is trying to recruit peacekeepers to separate the two sides but says a proper truce is a precondition.
Political mediation efforts are aimed at getting back on track presidential elections, due on July 27 but postponed due to the fighting.
Lissouba wants a constitutional council to extend his term of office until October because of the chaos. Sassou says the president is no longer fit to rule and must step down now.
